tagline.text: One of the largest Baroque churches in the Cagayan Valley, known as St. Peter Metropolitan Cathedral

location.label: Location
location.text: Rizal Street, Centro 10, Tuguegarao City (St. Peter's Cathedral complex)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100–500 (per person, local transport and snacks)

children.text: Tuguegarao Cathedral is a Baroque church built by the Dominicans in 1761–1768 and serves as the seat of the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao. Its densely ornamented brick facade and five-story bell tower are striking, and its location in the city center makes it a fitting first stop in Tuguegarao.

Tuguegarao Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church on Rizal Street in Centro 10, Tuguegarao City, and its official name is Saint Peter Metropolitan Cathedral. It is called a cathedral because it is the seat of the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao, and it counts among the larger Spanish colonial churches in the Cagayan Valley. Because it stands in the city center, it is easy to reach by tricycle from the airport or bus terminal, and it is a good place to visit before starting day trips such as Callao Cave or Iguig.

Its history goes back to May 9, 1604, when the Dominicans founded Tuguegarao as a mission town. The first priest, Tomás Villa, is said to have built a temporary church dedicated to Saints Peter and Paul. The present building was begun in 1761 under Fr. Antonio Lobato and completed in 1768. It was heavily damaged in World War II and its records were lost, but Bishop Constancio Jurgens rebuilt it. In 1982 the National Historical Institute, as it was then called, installed a historical marker, and in recent years restoration has been reported, repairing worn bricks and bringing back the original painted ceiling and altar decoration. The church is called a cathedral because the archbishop's seat is here. The Archdiocese of Tuguegarao is the center of a region that includes the dioceses of Bayombong and Ilagan and the Prelature of Batanes.

The architecture is known for a high, broad roof in what is called barn-style Baroque, with a richly decorated facade. The facade has an ornamental pediment that looks deliberately broken, and smooth pilasters alternate with twisted Solomonic ones. Around the windows and on the columns, molded bricks show roosters, papal tiaras, keys, the sun and moon, and Marian and Dominican symbols, which makes a close look rewarding. The five-story square bell tower on the left has blind windows at its base and a canopy and cross at the top. A short distance away is a Catholic cemetery with a brick arched entrance.

For travelers this is not a place to stay long but one to walk around for 1–2 hours while admiring the architecture. If you are a believer you can attend Mass and feel the atmosphere of the local community. In particular, the Sunday Mass at 7:30 a.m. is said to be celebrated in Ibanag, which makes it meaningful as a local cultural experience. However, Mass times and opening hours can change, so check the parish announcements before you go. Modest dress with shoulders and knees covered is the basic rule. The cathedral is close to the city center, which makes it a good reference point for a walking tour of Tuguegarao. Nearby are the brick chapel San Jacinto Ermita, said to have been built by the Dominicans in 1604, the Cagayan Museum and the restored Rizal Park, which you can link on foot in half a day. See the cathedral first and choose the rest according to the weather and your energy.

On the facade and bell tower, smooth and twisted pilasters alternate, and the bricks around the windows carry motifs such as roosters, papal tiaras, keys, and the sun and moon. Stand close and look up slowly. Photos work best in the morning or late afternoon, when each brick stands out and the shadows deepen the ornament.

A deeply recessed round window (oculus) at the center of the facade draws the eye, and the pediment above it appears deliberately broken. The form is also seen in a few churches in the Cagayan Valley and neighboring provinces.
A five-story square bell tower stands on the left of the church. The tradition of ringing the bells for the Angelus and for Mass is said to continue, so if you time your visit you can hear them.

Inside, work has been under way to repair worn bricks and restore the original painted ceiling and altar decoration. Depending on when you visit, there may be construction screens. The restoration has been funded by the parish priest and parishioners, so no completion date is fixed; check for news before you go.
The Sunday Mass at
is announced as celebrated in Ibanag. If you are a believer, attend quietly; if not, look around the interior outside Mass times.
The parish feast day is
June 29
. The area around the church can be crowded then, so check the schedule if you plan to visit.

There is a monument to the Sacred Heart of Jesus in front of the church, and the cathedral grounds are a good place to take photos and rest. Midday is very hot, so look for shade. Small shops and eateries across from the church and along nearby streets make it easy to take a break while walking.
A historical marker installed in 1982 explains the value of the church. If you read it before looking at the building, you can better sense the age of the church.

items.title: Half-day walk in Tuguegarao
items.subtitle: From the cathedral to the museum

children.text: Walk from your hotel in the city to the cathedral and look first at the brick-ornamented facade and the bell tower.
Look around the interior outside Mass times and walk once around the cathedral complex.
Walk to the city museum (Cagayan Museum) and Rizal Park, and eat pancit batil patong at a local restaurant.
Go to the Chapel of San Jacinto and see the building known as one of the oldest brick structures in the city. Check the opening hours locally.
Rest at your hotel or a cafe during the hottest hours, then see the cathedral again in the evening glow as the sun goes down.
Tuguegarao is known as one of the hottest cities in the Philippines, so keep outdoor plans in the middle of the day short.

items.title: Full-day church tour
items.subtitle: The cathedral and nearby pilgrimage sites

children.text: See the cathedral early and have a light breakfast.
Rent a car and go to Iguig Calvary Hills to see the Stations of the Cross and the church.
Walk along the Stations of the Cross sculptures on the hill behind Iguig Church and enjoy the view toward the river.
Have lunch, then go to Piat Basilica to pay your respects to the image of Our Lady.
Return to Tuguegarao and have dinner near the cathedral.
Rent the vehicle by the day and agree on the fare with the driver first.
The domestic flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG) takes about
1 hour
. Airlines and schedules change by season.
From the airport, take a taxi or tricycle to the city center; the cathedral is just one ride within the city.
Long-distance buses (such as Victory Liner and Five Star) run from Manila to Tuguegarao and take about
10–12 hours
From the Tuguegarao terminal, take a tricycle to the cathedral.
The distance between Manila and Tuguegarao is about
486km
. Check locally for last buses and night departures.
Tricycles are the most common; jeepneys and UV Express vans also run. In the city center you may also see kalesas (horse-drawn carriages).
Ask the fare before you ride, and for the cathedral complex tell the driver Rizal Street.
If you lose your way in the cathedral complex, use Rizal Street as your reference for direction. Avoid walking in the midday heat.
Tuguegarao is a hot, humid city. It is said to hold the Philippine record for the highest temperature (42.2 degrees, on May 11, 1969), and midday in March–May is hard to bear.
For walking, cool mornings in December–February are best, and the city festival Pavvurulun Afi in mid-August also offers plenty to see. However, lodging and transport get crowded then.
The parish feast day, June 29, falls on the border between the dry and rainy seasons, so showers are possible. If you want to see the celebration, bring an umbrella and book lodging early.

Tuguegarao has hotels and guesthouses in the city center and on the outskirts. Choosing a place within walking distance of the cathedral makes getting around easy, and if you plan day trips to the north, a place with good access to terminals and roads is suitable. Hotel names and rates change over time, so check recent reviews. Travelers looking for Korean food can use restaurants inside city malls, but in this region eating local food at pancit shops and longganisa stalls is more memorable. Restaurants get crowded right after the Sunday Mass, when mealtimes overlap.

Pancit batil patong is the signature dish. It is a local dish of noodles topped with stir-fried meat and an egg, served with an egg soup, and many pancit shops in the city sell it. The local longganisa, with a strong salty and garlicky flavor, is made with pork or carabao meat and is worth trying for breakfast. In hot weather a cold drink and a bowl of halo-halo help cool you down, and local cafes also serve as air-conditioned resting spots during the day.
Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, and avoid taking photos during Mass.
It is quieter to see the interior outside Mass times (weekdays in the early morning around 5–7 a.m. and several times on Sundays). Times can change, so check the parish announcements.
The closer you look at the brick ornament the more interesting it gets, so take photos when the sunlight comes in at an angle during the day.
Midday is very hot, so bring a hat, water and sunscreen.
The parish office is announced as closed on Mondays and holidays, so make any inquiries on another day.
The parish phone number is listed as (078) 844-1662. It may have changed, so also check social media announcements.
If you use a tripod or a drone for filming, it is best to ask permission in advance.
Some shops on the streets around the cathedral close after lunch, so buy snacks and drinks beforehand.
If you plan to visit pilgrimage sites nearby, renting a vehicle for the day is the efficient way to travel.
Check the fare before you ride around the city and keep small change ready.
Tuguegarao is very hot at midday. Move outdoor plans to early morning or evening and drink water often.
Mass times and parish office hours can change. Check the parish announcements before you go.
Some areas may be screened off because of restoration work.
Pickpockets and snatchers can be anywhere, so keep valuables in front of your body.
During religious services, refrain from photos and loud voices, and do not disturb worshippers' prayers.
During archdiocesan events or feast days, roads around the church may be closed and congested.
The city itself, where the cathedral stands, has the Chapel of San Jacinto, a museum and local food, all reachable on foot.
